POST /todoApp/admin/collaborationPermissions produces a valid permissionId; ensuring a created permission exists prevents update attempts against nonexistent ids and supports uniqueness checks when changing the `code`. If this prerequisite fails, the PUT will return 404 or a uniqueness conflict may be irrelevant.

operations.specification:
This operation performs a soft-deletion of a collaboration permission record in the Prisma model `todo_app_collaboration_permissions`. It targets the database table defined as `todo_app_collaboration_permissions` and implements the business rule to mark a permission record as deleted by setting its `deleted_at` timestamp rather than permanently removing the row. The operation ensures referential integrity is preserved while making the permission unavailable for normal collaborator assignment flows. Service consumers should use this endpoint when an administrative operator needs to retire a permission code from active use without losing the historical record for audit and compliance.

The implementation will update the `deleted_at` column on the targeted `todo_app_collaboration_permissions` row with the current timestamp. The operation must validate the identifier format (UUID) and verify the record exists and is not already soft-deleted. If the record is already soft-deleted the operation returns a suitable HTTP status indicating idempotent result. This operation requires elevated privileges and therefore is restricted to the `admin` actor. Related operations include listing permissions (`GET /collaborationPermissions`), retrieving a permission (`GET /collaborationPermissions/{permissionId}`), and a restore operation (not defined here) which would clear `deleted_at` to reinstate a permission.

Database mapping and implications: this operation maps to the Prisma model `todo_app_collaboration_permissions` whose notable columns include `id` (UUID primary key), `code` (unique permission code), `description` (human-friendly description), `is_grantable` (boolean indicating whether collaborators may be assigned the permission), `created_at` and `updated_at` timestamps, and `deleted_at` (nullable timestamptz used to mark soft-deletion). Because the Prisma model includes `deleted_at`, this operation implements soft-delete semantics by populating that column rather than performing a hard delete. Audit and compliance systems should continue to be able to reference the record after deletion via the `deleted_at` marker.

Validation and business rules: the path parameter `permissionId` must be a valid UUID that corresponds to `todo_app_collaboration_permissions.id`. The service will return 400 if the UUID format is invalid, 404 if no active or soft-deleted record exists for the id, or 409 if business constraints prevent deletion (for example, the permission is still referenced by a system-level invariant — caller should check preconditions via listing/assignment endpoints prior to deleting). On success the endpoint marks `deleted_at` and returns 204 No Content to indicate the operation completed and no further body is returned.

Security and authorization: only actors with administrative privileges may call this endpoint. The endpoint must perform an authorization check to ensure the caller is an `admin` and must record the action in `todo_app_audit_logs` including the acting admin id, session id, the target `todo_app_collaboration_permissions.id`, event_type `delete_permission`, and a textual reason when provided by the caller (stored in the audit trail; reason is not part of this endpoint payload but may be recorded by the invoking admin UI/workflow).
operations.summary: Soft-delete a collaboration permission (todo_app_collaboration_permissions) by marking its deleted_at timestamp
operations.description:
Purpose and overview:
This endpoint allows an administrator to retire a collaboration permission by marking the corresponding row in the `todo_app_collaboration_permissions` table as deleted. The operation maps directly to the Prisma model `todo_app_collaboration_permissions` and sets the `deleted_at` timestamp to indicate the permission is no longer active while preserving the record for audit and historical queries.

Security and permissions:
Access to this endpoint is restricted to administrative actors. The request must be authenticated and authorized as an `admin`. All successful and failed attempts to delete a permission MUST be recorded in the audit subsystem (`todo_app_audit_logs`) with `event_type` such as `delete_permission`, the acting admin id, session context, and the target permission id.

Relationship to database entity and fields:
This operation targets the `todo_app_collaboration_permissions` model which includes fields: `id` (UUID primary key), `code` (unique permission code), `description` (human-friendly text), `is_grantable` (boolean), `created_at`, `updated_at`, and `deleted_at` (nullable timestamptz). Because the model exposes `deleted_at`, the operation implements soft-delete semantics: it sets `deleted_at` to the current timestamp rather than removing the row.

Validation and business logic:
- The `permissionId` path parameter must be a valid UUID and correspond to an existing permission. If the format is invalid the API returns 400 Bad Request. If the permission does not exist or is already soft-deleted, the API returns 404 Not Found or 410 Gone depending on system policy; by default it will return 404 to avoid leaking existence.
- If a permission cannot be retired due to a business constraint (for example, it is referenced by immutable system configuration), the endpoint will return 409 Conflict with a clear reason.

Related operations and expected behavior:
Clients may call `GET /collaborationPermissions` to view all permissions or `GET /collaborationPermissions/{permissionId}` to inspect a single permission prior to deletion. A complementary restore endpoint (not implemented here) would clear `deleted_at` to reinstate a permission.

Error handling and idempotency:
- Calling this endpoint multiple times for the same `permissionId` is idempotent: once `deleted_at` is set, subsequent calls will return 204 and leave the record unchanged (or return 404/410 depending on policy). Any unexpected server error returns 500 with diagnostic details logged for operators.

operations.specification:
Permanently remove a collaboration permission identified by its globally-unique code from the `todo_app_collaboration_permissions` table. This operation maps to the Prisma model `todo_app_collaboration_permissions` and performs a hard delete because the provided schema for this model does not include a `deleted_at` field. If the product team prefers soft-delete semantics, update the Prisma model to add a nullable `deleted_at` column and update the implementation to set that field instead of deleting the row.

Business purpose: Administrative operators retire obsolete or incorrect permission codes so they can no longer be assigned to collaborators. Because deletion is permanent under the current schema, callers must confirm intent before invoking this endpoint.

Validation and business rules: The path parameter `permissionCode` must match `todo_app_collaboration_permissions.code` (global scope). The API validates existence and returns appropriate status codes: 204 (No Content) on success, 400 for malformed code, 404 if not found, 409 for business constraint conflicts, and 500 for internal errors. Audit logging (`todo_app_audit_logs`) must record the delete action transactionally with acting admin id and session id.
operations.summary: Permanently delete a collaboration permission by code
operations.description:
Purpose and overview:
This administrative endpoint permanently removes a collaboration permission identified by its globally-unique code from the `todo_app_collaboration_permissions` table. The current Prisma schema for this model does not include a `deleted_at` column; therefore this endpoint performs a hard delete. If the product decides on soft-delete semantics, the schema must be updated and the API changed accordingly.

Security and permissions:
Access is restricted to administrative actors. The server MUST verify the caller is an `admin` and MUST record the action in `todo_app_audit_logs` with `event_type = "delete_permission"`, including acting admin id and session id. Audit insertion should be transactional with deletion where possible.

Validation and errors:
- 204 No Content: deletion succeeded
- 400 Bad Request: malformed permission code
- 404 Not Found: permission code not found
- 409 Conflict: deletion blocked by business constraint
- 500 Internal Server Error: unexpected error

ITodoAppTodoUser.IAuthorized.description: Authorized response returned after successful login or refresh. Contains the authenticated user's id and token container; may include a non-sensitive user summary. Maps to the todo_app_todouser model for context; sensitive fields (password_hash, mfa_secret, mfa_backup_codes) are intentionally excluded.

id.description: Identifier of the authenticated user. Must match todo_app_todouser.id for the authenticated account.

email.description: Primary email address for the account. Returned for profile display and contact purposes.

display_name.description: Optional user-facing display name. Nullable when the user has not set a display name. Application trims surrounding whitespace; API returns null when no display name is set.

is_verified.description: Whether the user has verified their email address (true = verified).

status.description: Account lifecycle status. Possible values are defined by business logic (e.g., 'pending_verification','active','suspended','pending_deletion','deleted'). Returned exactly as stored in the database.

mfa_enabled.description: Whether multi-factor authentication (MFA) is enabled for this account (opt-in).

createdAt.description: Record creation timestamp in RFC3339 / ISO 8601 format.

updatedAt.description: Record last modification timestamp in RFC3339 / ISO 8601 format.

deletedAt.description: Soft-delete timestamp (nullable). Maps to todo_app_todouser.deleted_at. Included to maintain parity with other user DTOs and enable authorized callers to detect deleted accounts. Omitted or null for active accounts.

user.description: Optional non-sensitive summary information about the authenticated user.

ITodoAppTodoUser.ILogin.description: Login request for todoApp users. Clients submit credentials (email + password) along with session context (href and referrer). The server verifies password against the todo_app_todouser.password_hash. Session context fields (href, referrer) are required for self-login flows; ip is optional and may be null.

email.description: User email address used to identify the account. Maps to todo_app_todouser.email.

password.description: Plain-text user password. The server verifies this against todo_app_todouser.password_hash; clients MUST NOT send pre-hashed passwords. Minimum length 8 to align with password policy.

ip.description: Optional client IP address for session creation (nullable). Server may extract this automatically; include for SSR use-cases.

href.description: Connection URL (current page URL) where the login originated. Required for self-login session creation.

referrer.description: Referrer URL (previous page URL). Required for self-login session creation.

ITodoAppTodoUser.IRefresh.description: Refresh request payload containing a refresh token. The server validates the token's issuance time against todo_app_todouser.refresh_tokens_revoked_at to enforce revocation. The refresh token is a sensitive credential and clients MUST treat it as secret (transmit over TLS, store securely).

refresh_token.description: Refresh token previously issued by the authorization endpoint. The server will validate token issuance time against todo_app_todouser.refresh_tokens_revoked_at.

email.description: Email address of the account requesting a password reset. The server will look up the todo_app_todouser record by this address and, if present, persist an opaque, high-entropy password_reset_token (todo_app_todouser.password_reset_token) and set password_reset_expires_at (todo_app_todouser.password_reset_expires_at). The API MUST NOT return the stored token in the response; delivery is performed via out-of-band email. Example: "alice@example.com".

ITodoAppTodoUser.IPasswordResetRequest.description: Request DTO used to initiate a password reset for a todoApp user. Contains only the email used to identify the account. This DTO does not accept actor-identifying fields and does not expose any sensitive data. Implementation notes: issuing a reset SHOULD generate a single-use, high-entropy token, persist it to todo_app_todouser.password_reset_token, set todo_app_todouser.password_reset_expires_at to a near-future expiry (e.g., 1 hour), and send the token to the owner's verified email address. The endpoint response should be an acknowledgement only and must not include the token.

token.description: One-time password reset token previously issued to the user (matches todo_app_todouser.password_reset_token). Tokens are opaque, single-use, and time-limited; the server MUST validate the token value and expiry (password_reset_expires_at) and then clear the persisted token upon successful use. Example: "rt_7b1f4f2e-0a3b-4d6a-9c8d-abcdef123456".

password.description: New password in plain text. The server MUST validate strength according to policy, hash this value, and store the resulting value in todo_app_todouser.password_hash. On successful reset the server MUST nullify todo_app_todouser.password_reset_token and todo_app_todouser.password_reset_expires_at and set todo_app_todouser.refresh_tokens_revoked_at to the current timestamp to invalidate existing refresh tokens. Example: "N3wSecur3P@ss!".

ITodoAppTodoUser.IResetPassword.description: Request body to finalize a password reset for a todo user. The server validates the provided reset token and its expiry, replaces the stored password hash (todo_app_todouser.password_hash), clears the reset token fields, and rotates/invokes session revocation by updating refresh_tokens_revoked_at. This DTO MUST NOT include any actor identity fields and the API MUST NOT return password_hash or any secret material in responses.

ITodoAppTodoUser.IChangePassword.description: Authenticated request to change the caller's password. The server validates currentPassword against todo_app_todouser.password_hash, then sets password_hash to the hashed newPassword and updates refresh_tokens_revoked_at to revoke prior refresh tokens. This DTO MUST NOT accept or include any user id fields (actor identity is derived from the authenticated context). Audit/logging of the change is recommended (todo_app_user_activity_logs or todo_app_audit_logs).

currentPassword.description: Current password in plain text. Used by the server to verify the caller's identity before changing the password. Minimum length 8 characters. Server MUST NOT log this value.

newPassword.description: New password in plain text. The server MUST hash this value and persist it to todo_app_todouser.password_hash and update todo_app_todouser.refresh_tokens_revoked_at to the current timestamp to revoke prior refresh tokens. Minimum length 8 characters.

ITodoAppTodoUser.IEnableMfa.description: Request DTO to enable multi-factor authentication (MFA) for the currently authenticated todo user. This request is sent by an authenticated actor (authorizationActor: "todoUser"). The server will generate and persist the MFA secret and backup codes (stored encrypted in the Prisma model fields `mfa_secret` and `mfa_backup_codes`) and set `mfa_enabled` to true only after successful verification when requireVerification=true. The request object contains only non-sensitive provisioning preferences; the server MUST NOT return persisted secrets in responses. Audit logging of the change (todo_app_audit_logs / todo_app_user_activity_logs) is recommended.

provisioningMethod.description: Requested provisioning method. For MVP only the exact value 'totp' is supported (time-based one-time password). The server will generate the TOTP secret and provisioning URI (otpauth://) for the client to display as a QR code. Value MUST be exactly 'totp'.

oneOf.description: Optional human-friendly device label supplied by the client (e.g., "Personal iPhone"). Stored only for display in the user's session list or audit; do not include operating-system-specific identifiers.
Explicit null when the client intends to omit or clear the device label.

deviceName.description: Optional human-friendly device label supplied by the client (nullable).

requireVerification.description: If true the server will not finalize enabling MFA until the client verifies the provisioned secret (preferred flow). If false the server may enable provisioning and return provisioning data immediately. For security, the server SHOULD require verification before setting mfa_enabled=true. Default: true.

ITodoAppTodoUser.IDisableMfa.description:
Request DTO to disable multi-factor authentication (MFA) for the currently authenticated todo user.

This endpoint requires strong actor context (authorizationActor: "todoUser"). Disabling MFA is a sensitive operation and server implementations SHOULD require step-up verification (for example, current password confirmation or recent re-authentication). The server MUST clear or securely overwrite mfa_secret and mfa_backup_codes in the Prisma model and set mfa_enabled to false. Audit logs MUST record the action (todo_app_admin_actions or todo_app_audit_logs depending on actor). Returned responses MUST NOT include persisted secrets.

current_password.description: The actor's current password used for step-up verification. Required for this sensitive operation. The server MUST verify this value against the stored hash and MUST NOT echo it in any response. Use strong verification; consider rate-limiting and step-up policies.

revoke_backup_codes.description: When true, instructs the server to revoke any previously issued backup codes in addition to clearing the primary secret. When the server processes this flag it MUST remove or overwrite persisted backup codes (todo_app_todouser.mfa_backup_codes) and log the action in audit logs. Default: true.

sessionHandle.description: Optional session identifier or label for audit attribution. When provided it SHOULD be recorded in todo_app_user_activity_logs for traceability. This field is optional and may be null. DO NOT use this field to convey actor identity — actor is taken from authenticated context (JWT).

ITodoAppAdmin.description: Administrator account DTO (safe response). Returns non-sensitive administrative metadata from the todo_app_admin Prisma model. Sensitive fields such as password_hash, mfa_secret, and mfa_backup_codes are deliberately omitted.

id.description: Primary identifier of the administrator account. Maps to todo_app_admin.id from the Prisma schema.

email.description: Administrator login email (unique). Taken from todo_app_admin.email. This field is returned for audit and display purposes. NEVER include password_hash or other secrets.

display_name.description: Optional human-friendly display name for the admin (nullable). Maps to todo_app_admin.display_name.

role.description: Administrator role. Allowed exact values are defined by the IEAdminRole enum: 'moderator', 'support', 'superadmin'. Role values drive authorization decisions and UI affordances. Maps to todo_app_admin.role.

is_active.description: Whether the admin account is active and allowed to authenticate. Maps to todo_app_admin.is_active.

createdAt.description: Record creation timestamp (ISO 8601). Maps to todo_app_admin.created_at.

updatedAt.description: Record last modification timestamp (ISO 8601). Maps to todo_app_admin.updated_at.

deletedAt.description: Soft-delete timestamp (nullable). When non-null the record is soft-deleted. Maps to todo_app_admin.deleted_at.

ITodoAppAdmin.ICreate.description: Admin creation DTO used by the admin sign-up endpoint. Clients MUST provide a plaintext `password` (server will hash into Prisma's `password_hash`). This DTO intentionally excludes system-managed fields (id, createdAt, updatedAt, deletedAt) and sensitive storage fields (password_hash). For self-signup flows, session context fields are required: `href` and `referrer`. `ip` is optional. The server MUST trim and validate display_name when present.

email.description: Administrator email address. Must be unique (Prisma enforces uniqueness). Maps to todo_app_admin.email.

password.description: Plaintext password supplied by the client. The server MUST hash this value (never store plaintext) and MUST NOT log the plaintext password. Enforce password policy server-side (minimum length 8).

display_name.description: Optional human-friendly display name for the admin (nullable). Server SHOULD trim surrounding whitespace and enforce a sensible maximum length (e.g., 250 chars). Maps to todo_app_admin.display_name.

oneOf.description: Administrator role: moderator.
Administrator role: support.
Administrator role: superadmin.
Null when role not provided; server may apply default role or require approval.

role.description: Optional initial role for the admin. Allowed values: 'moderator', 'support', 'superadmin'. Server MUST validate and reject any value outside this set. Maps to todo_app_admin.role.

ip.description: Client IP address for session creation (OPTIONAL - server may extract it). Nullable when client does not supply it. Used for audit/session attribution; maps to session.ip, not persisted directly on admin row.

href.description: Connection URL (current page URL) where the sign-up originated. Required for self-signup flows to populate session metadata and create an initial session record. Used for audit context and session creation.

referrer.description: Referrer URL (previous page URL). Required for self-signup flows to populate session metadata and create an initial session record. Used for audit context and session creation.

ITodoAppAdmin.ISummary.description: Lightweight summary of an administrator account. Maps to Prisma model `todo_app_admin`. Intended for embedding in audit and admin-action summaries. Contains identifying and role information only — no secrets or hashed credentials are exposed. Timestamps use camelCase in API responses and map to the underlying Prisma timestamp columns.

id.description: Administrator unique identifier. Maps to todo_app_admin.id.

email.description: Administrator login email (maps to todo_app_admin.email). Returned for audit and display purposes. NEVER include password_hash or other secrets.

displayName.description: Optional human-friendly display name for the admin (nullable). Maps to todo_app_admin.display_name.

oneOf.description: Administrator role or scope identifier. Allowed values: 'moderator', 'support', 'superadmin'. Maps to todo_app_admin.role.
Administrator role or scope identifier. Allowed values: 'moderator', 'support', 'superadmin'. Maps to todo_app_admin.role.
Administrator role or scope identifier. Allowed values: 'moderator', 'support', 'superadmin'. Maps to todo_app_admin.role.

role.description: Administrator role or scope identifier. Allowed values: 'moderator', 'support', 'superadmin'. Maps to todo_app_admin.role.

isActive.description: Whether the admin account is active and allowed to authenticate. Maps to todo_app_admin.is_active.

createdAt.description: Record creation timestamp (ISO 8601). Maps to todo_app_admin.created_at.

updatedAt.description: Record last modification timestamp (ISO 8601). Maps to todo_app_admin.updated_at. Nullable when not present.

deletedAt.description: Soft-delete timestamp; null when active. Maps to todo_app_admin.deleted_at. Inclusion in responses MUST be authorization-gated to avoid leaking deletion status to unauthorized callers.

ITodoAppAdmin.IAuthorized.description: Authorized admin response. Contains minimal admin identity and authorization tokens. Maps to the todo_app_admin Prisma model. Sensitive fields such as password_hash are explicitly excluded. NOTE: API uses camelCase for timestamp properties (createdAt/updatedAt/deletedAt); server maps these to the underlying Prisma snake_case columns.

id.description: Unique identifier of the authenticated admin (maps to todo_app_admin.id).

email.description: Administrator email address (maps to todo_app_admin.email). Returned for client display and audit context.

display_name.description: Human-friendly name for the admin (maps to todo_app_admin.display_name). Nullable when not set.

role.description: Administrator role or scope (maps to todo_app_admin.role). Use this value to drive client UI and server-side authorization decisions.

is_active.description: Whether the admin account is active and allowed to authenticate. Maps to todo_app_admin.is_active.

createdAt.description: Account creation timestamp (ISO 8601). Server maps this to todo_app_admin.created_at.

updatedAt.description: Record last modification timestamp (ISO 8601). Server maps this to todo_app_admin.updated_at.

deletedAt.description: Soft-delete timestamp (nullable). When non-null the record is soft-deleted. Server maps this to todo_app_admin.deleted_at.

ITodoAppAdmin.ILogin.description: Admin login request. Contains credentials and required session context fields (href, referrer). Do NOT include password_hash or any other persisted secret. Password policy: minlength 8 enforced for consistent client validation.

email.description: Administrator email address used for authentication. Must match the todo_app_admin.email value.

password.description: Administrator plaintext password (sent only for authentication). Minimum length 8 to match platform password policy. The server verifies this against the stored password_hash; the password MUST NOT be returned in any response.

ip.description: Client IP address for session recording and audit. Optional: server may extract IP if omitted.

href.description: Connection URL (current page URL) where the login originates. Required for session context and audit records.

referrer.description: Referrer URL (previous page URL) for session context and audit. Required for session context and audit records.

ITodoAppAdmin.IRefresh.description: Admin refresh request. Provide a valid refresh token to obtain a new access token (and optionally a rotated refresh token). The server MUST validate the token, ensure the referenced admin account exists, that todo_app_admin.is_active is true, and that todo_app_admin.deleted_at is null. The server SHOULD also check for token revocation/issuance markers and record successful and failed attempts in audit logs (todo_app_audit_logs) or user activity logs for traceability. The refresh token is an opaque credential and MUST be treated as sensitive by clients and servers (transmit only over TLS, do not log).

refresh_token.description: Refresh token string or token handle previously issued by the authentication service. The server validates this token, checks revocation/issued-at constraints, and issues a new access token (and optionally a rotated refresh token). Treat as opaque and sensitive.

ITodoAppSystemSetting.description: Full representation of a system configuration setting from the `todo_app_system_settings` Prisma model. Includes the serialized `value` payload which may contain JSON, boolean or numeric encoded as string. THIS SCHEMA IS ADMIN-SENSITIVE: the `value` field may contain operational configuration and MUST be returned only to authorized administrative actors. Access to this endpoint/field SHOULD be audited and subject to RBAC. Treat `deletedAt` as the soft-delete marker; by default return only records where deletedAt is null unless caller has explicit forensic privileges.

id.description: Unique identifier of the system setting (Prisma: todo_app_system_settings.id).

value.description: Serialized setting value stored as string. May contain JSON, boolean or numeric encoded as string. Because values can be sensitive (feature toggles, thresholds, credentials pointers), servers MUST only return this field to authorized administrative actors and SHOULD redact or mask when presenting in non-admin summaries.

description.description: Human-friendly description explaining purpose and acceptable values for the setting. Nullable when not provided.

isPublic.description: Whether this setting is visible to non-admin audiences (e.g., public telemetry or informational flags). Maps to todo_app_system_settings.is_public.

createdAt.description: Record creation timestamp (UTC). Maps to todo_app_system_settings.created_at.

updatedAt.description: Record last modification timestamp (UTC). Maps to todo_app_system_settings.updated_at.

deletedAt.description: Soft-delete timestamp; null when active. When non-null the record is considered deleted and should be treated as absent by normal admin lists unless forensic access is requested.

id.description: Unique identifier of the system setting (Primary Key). Maps to todo_app_system_settings.id.

key.description: Canonical setting key (unique). Examples: 'maintenance_mode', 'default_list_visibility'. Used as primary display identifier in summaries.

value.description: Serialized setting value stored as a string. Consumers interpret format (boolean, JSON, numeric) based on the key. SENSITIVE: this field MAY contain operational or configuration secrets and MUST only be returned to authorized administrative callers. For non-admin callers the API MUST redact or omit this property.

description.description: Human-friendly description explaining purpose and acceptable values for the setting. May be null.

isPublic.description: Whether this setting is visible to non-admin audiences (e.g., telemetry or informational flags).

createdAt.description: Record creation timestamp (UTC). Maps to todo_app_system_settings.created_at.

updatedAt.description: Record last modification timestamp (UTC). Maps to todo_app_system_settings.updated_at.

deletedAt.description: Soft-delete timestamp; null when active. Maps to todo_app_system_settings.deleted_at.

ITodoAppSystemSetting.ISummary.description: Administrative summary view for a system configuration setting. Provides minimal fields necessary for listing and identification in admin UIs. Maps to Prisma model 'todo_app_system_settings'. Timestamps included and required to support sorting and audit workflows. Note: the `value` field may be sensitive and must be authorization-gated.

ITodoAppSystemSetting.IRequest.description: Request DTO for searching and paginating system settings. Used by admin search endpoints. Supports exact `key`, prefix match on `key`, boolean filter on `isPublic`, full-text search against `description`, pagination, sorting, and an explicit includeDeleted flag for forensic queries. All API-facing field names use camelCase.

page.description: Page number (1-based). If omitted, server default applies.

pageSize.description: Number of items per page. Server may enforce a maximum; 100 is recommended upper bound.

key.description: Exact match filter for the setting key.

keyPrefix.description: Prefix match on the canonical key (returns keys that start with this value).

isPublic.description: Filter by visibility. When true, only public settings are returned; when false, only non-public settings are returned.

search.description: Full-text search string applied against the `description` field (Prisma gin_trgm_ops enabled).

oneOf.description: Field to sort by. Allowed values: 'createdAt', 'updatedAt', 'key'. Default: 'createdAt'.
Field to sort by. Allowed values: 'createdAt', 'updatedAt', 'key'. Default: 'createdAt'.
Field to sort by. Allowed values: 'createdAt', 'updatedAt', 'key'. Default: 'createdAt'.

sortBy.description: Field to sort by. Allowed values: 'createdAt', 'updatedAt', 'key'. Default: 'createdAt'.

oneOf.description: Sort direction. Allowed values: 'asc' or 'desc'. Default: 'asc'.
Sort direction. Allowed values: 'asc' or 'desc'. Default: 'asc'.

sortOrder.description: Sort direction. Allowed values: 'asc' or 'desc'. Default: 'asc'.

includeDeleted.description: When true and caller has forensic privileges, include rows with non-null deletedAt. Default: false. Note: honoring this flag requires admin-level authorization and MUST trigger audit logging.

ITodoAppFeatureFlag.description: Feature flag entity mapped to the Prisma model `todo_app_feature_flags` (admin-facing). Represents a platform feature toggle with rollout controls and admin-facing metadata. Field names use camelCase in the API; server maps these to the underlying Prisma columns (e.g., rolloutPercentage -> rollout_percentage). This DTO is intended for administrative detail views and must only be returned to authorized admin callers.

id.description: Primary key (UUID) of the feature flag record. Maps to todo_app_feature_flags.id.

key.description: Canonical unique key for the feature flag (e.g., "new_onboarding_flow"). Maps to todo_app_feature_flags.key.

enabled.description: Global enabled state of the feature flag. True when the feature is globally enabled. Maps to todo_app_feature_flags.enabled.

oneOf.description: Optional staged rollout percentage value between 0 and 100 (inclusive). Maps to Prisma column rollout_percentage.
Null when no staged rollout is configured.

rolloutPercentage.description: Optional staged rollout percentage (0..100). Nullable when not used. Use integer percent values (e.g., 25).

oneOf.description: Administrative description and notes for the feature flag. Use this field to explain intent, rollout guidance, or operational constraints. Intended for admin UIs; do not store secrets here.
Null when no description is provided.

description.description: Human-facing administrative description for the feature flag. Use this text to explain the flag's purpose, rollout guidance, operational considerations (for example: expected impact, recommended monitoring thresholds), and any special handling notes (e.g., whether the feature interacts with sensitive systems). This field is intended for admin UIs and operator documentation; it SHOULD NOT contain secrets or sensitive configuration data. When null, no description has been provided for the flag.

createdAt.description: Record creation timestamp in RFC3339 / ISO 8601 format. Maps to todo_app_feature_flags.created_at.

updatedAt.description: Record last modification timestamp in RFC3339 / ISO 8601 format. Maps to todo_app_feature_flags.updated_at.

oneOf.description: Soft-delete timestamp indicating when the record was marked deleted. Maps to todo_app_feature_flags.deleted_at.
Null when the record is active (not soft-deleted).

deletedAt.description: Soft-delete timestamp; when present indicates the record has been soft-deleted and may be excluded from default admin lists.

ITodoAppFeatureFlag.IRequest.description: Request schema for searching, filtering, sorting and paginating feature flags for administrative list endpoints. Validation rules: rolloutPercentageMin/Max must be integers in 0..100 when present; page and pageSize must be positive integers. Date filters must be RFC3339 date-time strings. Defaults applied: page=1, pageSize=25, includeDeleted=false. Use 1-based paging.

key.description: Optional partial or exact match for the feature flag key. Implementations SHOULD perform case-insensitive partial match for convenience (server decides exact matching rules).

rolloutPercentageMin.description: Optional minimum rollout percentage (inclusive). Must be integer between 0 and 100. Non-integer or out-of-range values MUST be rejected with 400.

rolloutPercentageMax.description: Optional maximum rollout percentage (inclusive). Must be integer between 0 and 100. Non-integer or out-of-range values MUST be rejected with 400.

createdAtFrom.description: Optional lower bound (inclusive) for createdAt timestamp (RFC3339).

createdAtTo.description: Optional upper bound (inclusive) for createdAt timestamp (RFC3339).

updatedAtFrom.description: Optional lower bound (inclusive) for updatedAt timestamp (RFC3339).

updatedAtTo.description: Optional upper bound (inclusive) for updatedAt timestamp (RFC3339).

includeDeleted.description: When true, include soft-deleted records (deletedAt IS NOT NULL) in results. Default: false.

page.description: 1-based page number for pagination. Must be a positive integer. Default: 1.

pageSize.description: Number of items per page. Must be a positive integer. Server SHOULD enforce a sensible maximum (100) to protect the backend. Default: 25.

oneOf.description: Sort by feature flag key (alpha).
Sort by createdAt timestamp (camelCase field name). Default: createdAt.
Sort by updatedAt timestamp (camelCase field name).
Sort by rolloutPercentage (camelCase mapping of rollout_percentage).

sortBy.description: Field to sort by. Allowed values: 'key','createdAt','updatedAt','rolloutPercentage'. Default: 'createdAt'.

oneOf.description: Sort direction. Allowed values: 'asc' or 'desc'. Default: 'asc'.
Sort direction. Allowed values: 'asc' or 'desc'. Default: 'asc'.

order.description: Sort direction. Allowed values: 'asc' or 'desc'. Default: 'asc'.

id.description: Unique identifier of the feature flag (Prisma: todo_app_feature_flags.id).

key.description: Canonical feature flag key. Example: "new_onboarding_flow" (Prisma: todo_app_feature_flags.key).

enabled.description: Global enabled/disabled state for the feature flag (Prisma: todo_app_feature_flags.enabled).

oneOf.description: Optional staged rollout percentage (0-100). When present, indicates the percent of the population targeted by the feature rollout. Maps to Prisma `rollout_percentage`.
Null indicates no staged rollout is configured.

rolloutPercentage.description: Optional staged rollout percentage (0-100) used by rollout systems. Null when not applicable (Prisma: todo_app_feature_flags.rollout_percentage).

oneOf.description: Human-friendly description for maintainers and admins. Use this field to explain intent, rollout guidance, or operational constraints. Avoid placing secrets here.
Null when no description is provided.

description.description: Administrative description and notes for the feature flag used in admin UI. Provides operational guidance for maintainers; do not include secrets or sensitive operational data.

createdAt.description: Record creation timestamp in RFC3339 format (Prisma: todo_app_feature_flags.created_at).

updatedAt.description: Record last modification timestamp in RFC3339 format (Prisma: todo_app_feature_flags.updated_at). This field exists in the Prisma model and has been added to the summary to reflect DB completeness.

oneOf.description: Soft-delete timestamp indicating when the record was marked deleted. Nullable in normal admin summaries. Maps to Prisma `deleted_at`.
Null when the record is active (not soft-deleted).

deletedAt.description: Soft-delete timestamp; when present indicates the record has been soft-deleted and may be excluded from default admin lists.

ITodoAppFeatureFlag.ISummary.description: Summary representation of a platform feature flag. Exposes identifying key, enabled state, optional rollout metadata, and timestamps. Maps to the Prisma model todo_app_feature_flags. Field names use camelCase to align with request DTO naming conventions.

limit.description: Maximum items per page (bounded by server maximum).

query.description: Full-text search string applied to title and description (max 256 chars).

oneOf.description: Filter lists by visibility. Allowed values: 'private','shared-invite-only','public'.

Filter lists by visibility. Allowed values: 'private','shared-invite-only','public'.

oneOf.description: Field to sort by. Allowed values: 'createdAt','title'. Default: createdAt.
Field to sort by. Allowed values: 'createdAt','title'. Default: createdAt.

ITodoAppList.IRequest.description: Query parameters for searching and paginating todo lists. This request schema is used for list retrieval endpoints and maps to the `todo_app_lists` model for filtering purposes. Note: authentication context is required for owner/collaborator scopes; private lists will never be returned to unauthorized callers.

title.description: List title. Required. Application trims surrounding whitespace and enforces a max length of 250 characters.

The service MUST normalize the `name` (trim surrounding whitespace and apply case-normalization policy) before persistence and must enforce uniqueness against active (non-soft-deleted) tags. On uniqueness conflict, the API SHOULD return 409 Conflict with a machine-readable error explaining the name collision. The database populates id and timestamps (created_at, updated_at).
